content:
Anya: FYI the ceres-q4b canary is surfacing NDJSON parse hiccups for funcall outputs, concentrated on longer completions (>512 tokens). Seen in ~6.9% of canary calls this morning.

Sam: got the alert. baseline raven-v2 was ~0.7% on same workload, so delta is sizable. dataset = 10k requests from 06:00-07:00 UTC.

Drew: any obvious generation patterns? commas, trailing bits, or streaming splits?

Anya: 90% of failures show trailing commas between lines or extra commas after objects. examples from snaps: 
```
{"tool":"apply_patch","patch":"@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@\n+..."},{"tool":"run_tests","cmd":"pytest tests/test_patch.py"},
```
The trailing comma causes our per-line JSON.parse to blow up.

Lin: sounds like the model template is generating NDJSON with separators but still appending commas. Could be the tokenization boundary adds a comma token.

Olivia: do we have token-level snaps? helpful to know if comma is separate token or concatenated.

Anya: uploaded samples to s3://redwood-canary/ceres/q4b/snaps/mar20-2026.jsonl. inspection shows "," is frequently its own token at line end, sometimes duplicated.

Sam: mitigation ideas:
- "soft_repair": tolerant line parser that strips trailing commas and runs a repair pass (regex + JSON.parse try)
- "array_wrap": wrap lines into an array and parse as JSON array then validate elements
- "rescue_model": call a small, low-cost model with a strict instruction to re-render valid NDJSON (fallback only)

Drew: tradeoffs: soft_repair is fast but could merge/alter semantics; rescue_model is more expensive (latency + tokens) but safer.

Lin: propose pipeline: try strict per-line parse -> if fail, run soft_repair -> if parse ok but schema invalid OR repair flagged suspicious, invoke rescue_model. Gate rescue by per-request token_budget and global QPS cap.

Olivia: define telemetry so we can measure impact: fields: repair_applied (true/false), rescue_called (true/false), repair_reason (trailing_comma|duplicate_comma|stream_boundary|escape_issue), semantic_check_pass (true/false), repair_confidence (low|med|high).

Anya: ran a 2h split test yesterday with 3 variants (1% each):
- strict (baseline): parse_success 93.1%
- soft_repair only: parse_success 98.2%, semantic_check_pass 97.5%
- soft_repair + rescue (rescue on schema fail): parse_success 99.1%, semantic_check_pass 99.0% but p95 latency increased +170ms and token cost +2.7%

Sam: those numbers look promising. Where are the semantic mismatches in soft_repair?

Anya: manual spot-check (n=60) found 3 cases where soft_repair merged two objects when a comma belonged to an inner array boundary, so repair introduced structural change.

Drew: can we tune the soft_repair heuristics to be more conservative (only strip single trailing comma, avoid line merges) and rely on rescue for ambiguous cases?

Lin: yes. change heuristics: remove repeated trailing commas, trim whitespace, don't join lines unless explicit evidence. Also add stream-boundary unit tests: case where a tokenized stream ends with a partial token that later supplies the comma.

Olivia: dashboard plan: per-route tiles for parse_rate, repair_rate, rescue_rate, p95_latency_delta, token_cost_delta, semantic_pass_rate. Also allow filtering by route tag so we can see high-impact routes (e.g., code-editor.apply_patch).

Anya: added route propagation so telemetry includes route_name. early data: apply_patch route accounts for ~58% of failures.

Sam: cost control: set per-request rescue token cap = 256 tokens and global rescue QPS cap = 4 per canary shard. Failures beyond cap go to human review queue.

Drew: also watch KV cache and resume/streaming behavior; need to ensure chunked responses don't create artificial commas across boundaries. add a streaming harness test emitting object boundary mid-chunk.

Lin: will add that test to the streaming test suite and a mock that simulates a resume with ','.

Anya: PR created with parser + telemetry + canary config: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/6187. includes unit tests and the soft_repair toggle behind feature flag.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: ceres-q4b -> infra-canary-2 (1% traffic) at ts=3134004322.

Drew: plan for tomorrow 07:00 UTC: run a 3-way 1% split for 2h, then an extended 6h run if soft_repair shows low semantic drift. Assignments: @Olivia (dashboards + route tagging), @Lin (rescue prompt + stream tests), @Sam (cost impact analysis), @Anya (parser PR + extended canary orchestration).

Olivia: will add dashboard alerts for semantic_pass_rate drop >2% and rescue_rate >0.5%.

Sam: if soft_repair reduces failures by >75% with semantic_pass_rate loss <1.5%, we can flip it on behind feature flag for all canaries.

Anya: agreed. next: run the 3-way smoke tomorrow, collect confusion snaps, add failing cases to the unit tests, and iterate heuristics.

Lin: logging note 1: ensure we log repair_diff (small diff of before/after JSON) for sampled repairs so we can audit dangerous changes.

Drew: excellent. reconvene after smoke. Thanks all :robot_face: :rocket:

deploy-bot: initial 1% observation period completed. flagged delta and awaiting operator to kick off 3-way split.
